title: Stripes: The Mutts of Basic Training
description: A worst day ever, a drill sergeant, a recruit named Psycho, and a very strange RV—five steps into Bill Murray's boot camp.
imageHint: Military boot camp scene with comedic chaos, drill sergeant, and recruits in formation

questions.question: Cabbie John Winger loses his job, car, apartment, and girlfriend in one day, so he talks his buddy Russell into joining what?
questions.explanation: Ivan Reitman pitched it after Meatballs. Harold Ramis tailored the script to Bill Murray and cast himself as Russell to help lure Murray in.

questions.question: In Army basic training, the platoon's tough drill instructor is played by Western legend Warren Oates. What's his name?
questions.explanation: Oates, a veteran of Peckinpah films like The Wild Bunch, gives the comedy its spine. It was one of his last major roles; he died the following year.

questions.question: Hulka meets a recruit called Psycho, who'll kill anyone who touches his stuff or uses his real first name. Hulka's reply: "Lighten up," what?
questions.explanation: The full line: "Lighten up, Francis. We're all in this together." Psycho is a not-so-subtle riff on Taxi Driver's Travis Bickle. Elmo is Judge Reinhold's recruit.

questions.question: With Hulka injured, Francis and the misfits train themselves overnight. At graduation, a general asks if it's true. What does Winger shout back?
questions.explanation: The decoys are real lines from the same scene; "Blown up, sir!" is where Hulka went. Murray improvised freely, and this line named a 40th-anniversary featurette.

questions.question: "That's the fact, Jack!" wins the general over, and he assigns the platoon to guard his top-secret weapon, disguised as an RV. What's it called?
questions.explanation: It's basically an armed GMC Motorhome. Three years later, Reitman, Murray, and Ramis traded it for a converted Cadillac ambulance called Ecto-1.

easterEgg.title: Cheech & Chong Go to the Army
easterEgg.text: Reitman first pitched Stripes as a military comedy for Cheech & Chong. The stoner duo became two slackers instead, and the project went to Bill Murray.
